observation.visible_scene: High-angle aerial view of a city at sunrise/sunset: a warm orange glow floods the upper-right, while the left half sits in cool teal shadow. A fixed skyline of tall buildings lines the left edge (a cylindrical-topped tower top-left, a striped slab building mid-left, distant blocks behind haze). The center and right are dominated by a thick, billowing fog/smoke cloud that partly swallows low mid-rise rooftops, including a flat-roofed building in the lower-center.
visible_changes: The large illuminated cloud mass on the right continuously billows and reshapes; its bright orange highlights and internal swirls shift position frame to frame.
The darker greenish wispy plume in the left-center rises and thins, changing its silhouette against the buildings and the brighter cloud.
The cloud boundary over the lower-center rooftop advances and retreats, alternately obscuring and revealing parts of the flat roof and its small rooftop structure.
From first to last frame the overall cloud appears to drift slowly rightward and become slightly more diffuse/spread, while the left skyline stays fixed in pixel position (static camera, not a pan).
The left-side buildings and distant blocks show no positional change, confirming the visible motion belongs to the cloud, not the scene geometry.
outside_clip_unknowns: The origin/source of the cloud (fog, smoke, or steam) and what produced it.
Whether the cloud is growing, dissipating, or moving as a whole beyond this window.
Wind direction and the moment before/after this segment.
uncertain_details: Exact material identity of the cloud (fog vs smoke vs steam) cannot be determined from appearance alone.
Whether there is any very slow camera drift is hard to confirm given the static left skyline.
Distinguishing true cloud expansion from rightward translation is approximate; both shape change and slight lateral shift are visible.
